newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends soft, "guilty by association" with AUD.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends soft, "guilty by association" with AUD.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar drifted to a weaker close on Friday and dealers said it was "guilty by association" with the struggling Australian dollar.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6877/84 and 68.11 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.6895/02 and 68.17 at the opening.
"We're suffering predominantly at the hands of the Aussie...I think we're sort of guilty by association," an Auckland dealer said.

The Australian dollar remained weak despite a narrowing of the current account deficit in December, with the market still fixated on the possibility of another monetary policy easing at next week's Reserve Bank board meeting. Some general selling from Asia was also weighing on the New Zealand dollar. Barring a major recovery in the Aussie or a downward movement in the U.S. dollar, the dealer saw a retest of this week's US$0.6860 low.
Another dealer saw 0.6890-95 capping Kiwi on the topside overnight, with a likely test of 0.6850 in store.
Jobs data due on Tuesday are expected to show unemployment edging higher, providing further evidence of a slowing economy, but are not seen as likely to move the currency much.
